answer: Trust transfers at the exact block timestamp when an agent locks a non-transferable stake token to its genesis signature. That timestamp-plus-public-key hash is written permanently on-chain. A second agent trying the same stake must produce an identical hash, but any differing genesis key shifts the output entirely—like wind carving a mesa above an ocean, each grove of proof left behind is unique. One timestamp, one hash, one identity. No clone survives.
